cards.headline: US launches limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island

pages.text: The United States launched limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island late on November 2, 2026, targeting missile batteries used against US assets. The strikes, which were disclosed by Iranians on social media and confirmed by US Central Command (Centcom), occurred hours after US Vice President JD Vance expressed optimism that diplomatic efforts to end the war were moving in the right direction. The US described the strikes as defensive in nature, aimed at surface-to-air missiles used in attacks against US planes the day before. This was the first attack on Qeshm Island since June. The island, located off Iran’s southern coast, serves as a primary platform for Iran’s asymmetric naval power. While blame was initially placed on Israel by those inside Iran, it was later conceded that the US was responsible; Israel insisted it had no role in the attacks.

The military action comes as diplomatic mediators attempt to prevent a return to all-out war. Mediation efforts led by Qatar have involved passing messages between the US and Iran through indirect talks. On November 2, 2026, Qatari mediators traveled to Tehran to meet with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi regarding a draft US-Iran deal that has been under negotiation for eight days. Although an Iranian delegation departed Doha on November 1, 2026, a draft proposal is still being circulated. Araghchi stated that consultations are intensive and that the outcome depends on the political rationality of Washington. Mediators believe it will be clear within two days whether a basis for continued indirect talks exists.

The strikes occurred on the eve of US midterm elections. The US has attempted to downplay the significance of the attacks, stating they are not the precursor to a major assault on Iran that Donald Trump has promised after the midterms if the US determines Iran’s nuclear program remains a threat to the West. Iran’s deputy foreign minister, Kazem Gharibabadi, said the country remains in a state of war and maintains the right to legitimate defense. Iranian chief negotiator Mohammad Ghalibaf told parliament that any miscalculation by the US would lead to an unpredictable Iranian response. Similar military exchanges have occurred at least three times since the cessation of major hostilities as the US and Iran compete for control of the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: Three injured in attack on student assembly at University of Athens campus

pages.text: Three people were injured when a group of individuals, some wearing helmets, attacked a student assembly at the University of Athens campus in Greece, according to Greece’s medical emergency service and the semi-state Athens News Agency. The three injured individuals were treated at an Athens hospital for injuries that were not critical, the emergency service said. Police are investigating the incident, though it was not immediately clear who carried out the attack or why. No arrests were immediately reported.

The Greek Education Ministry condemned the violence, stating the attack “insulted the academic community and undermined freedom of expression.” The incident occurred amid broader unrest, as thousands of students and teachers have taken to the streets across Greece to demand higher state funding for education, better facilities, and less-crowded classrooms. Student groups have planned further demonstrations.

cards.headline: Oil prices rise amid Iran war uncertainty and US midterm election results

pages.text: Oil prices rose during a volatile session as investors monitored potential shifts in US policy following midterm elections, in which Democrats captured control of both houses of the US Congress from President Donald Trump’s Republicans. Brent futures rose 82 cents, or 0.8 percent, to $104.42 a barrel at 08:10 a.m., while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained 50 cents, or 0.5 percent, to $96.59, reversing earlier declines. This price movement follows a previous session where Brent settled at its lowest level in nearly four weeks as traders weighed ongoing talks to end conflicts in Ukraine and Iran. Following the elections, President Trump admitted that the war with Iran contributed to Republican losses and vowed to veto what he described as “insane” legislation.

Market uncertainty is driven by the ongoing conflict between the US and Iran. A US official stated that the US had carried out “defensive” strikes on Iran’s Qeshm island, targeting surface-to-air missiles used against US assets, though another official noted the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations. Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insights at Phillip Nova, said President Trump’s conflicting signals—continuing military strikes while simultaneously downplaying further escalation—have made it difficult for traders to establish strong directional conviction. Despite these signals, Sachdeva noted that underlying supply disruption risks around the Strait of Hormuz remain, and an unexpected drawdown in US crude inventories is providing fundamental support to prices.

Diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict continue as Qatar has stepped up mediation to prevent an escalation of attacks following the US elections. However, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on November 3, 2026, that Iran and the US remain far from a deal to end their war. Markets continue to monitor any progress in negotiations regarding the US-Israeli war with Iran.

cards.headline: Democrats win majorities in US House and Senate in 2026 midterm elections

pages.text: Democrats have won clear majorities in both the US House of Representatives and the Senate during the 2026 midterm elections, according to reports from DW and the Associated Press. While vote counts were still ongoing at the time of reporting, the results represent a shift from before election night, when Republicans held majorities in both chambers of Congress, if only by a narrow margin. In the Senate, Democrats crossed the 51-seat threshold required to gain control of the chamber by flipping several Republican seats, including races in North Carolina, South Carolina, Kansas, Texas, and Iowa. The 2026 midterms involved Americans voting for all 435 members of the House of Representatives and 35 members of the Senate. Because the US Constitution delegates significant executive power to the presidency, but requires Congress to approve the majority of federal political decisions before implementation, these results are expected to influence US politics for the next few years.

International media and leaders have reacted to the election results, which several outlets characterized as a significant shift in US political power. The French newspaper Libération described the win as 'une vague bleue' (a blue wave), while Britain's Daily Mail called it a 'historic blue tsunami.' The Times of India ran the headline 'midterm blues for Trump.' In Israel, following its own parliamentary elections, the Times of Israel focused on the triumph of Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, while Haaretz reported that El-Sayed's victory showed that opposition to Israel is not a barrier to winning battleground states. In North America, newspapers in Canada and Mexico noted the results as a setback and rebuke for Trump. While international leaders often avoid commenting directly on midterm results, several have made public statements regarding this election.

Global reactions also reflected concerns regarding international conflicts and security. The Kyiv Independent expressed hope that the Democratic control of Congress would provide a potential boost for Ukraine. Conversely, the Russian state-run daily Rossiyskaya Gazeta suggested the results would be a blow to Ukraine and predicted that Trump's wrath would fall on Europe following the Republican defeat. Iran's Tehran Times used the phrase 'Operation Midterms Hammer,' referencing a U.S. military strike against Iran in June 2025. These geopolitical tensions follow the renewal of the war between the United States and Israel against Iran in February, an event that pushed up the prices of oil and other goods and became a major issue during the election campaign.

cards.headline: NBA removes Rwandan army team from African league following US sanctions

pages.text: The National Basketball Association (NBA) has removed the Armée Patriotique Rwandaise (APR), a Rwandan army-funded club, from its Basketball Africa League (BAL). The NBA stated the decision follows US sanctions imposed on Rwanda in March. While the association had previously announced that the APR would not participate in the 2026 BAL, this is the first time the NBA has disclosed the reasons for the removal. The APR, which previously placed third in the league, is part of Rwanda, which is an official BAL partner and pays the league to host its finals at the 10,000-seat BK Arena in Kigali.

The NBA's decision follows a letter sent on 23 October to the association by Democratic Senator Jeffrey Merkley and Republican Senator Marsha Blackburn. The senators requested that the NBA reconsider its partnership with the Rwandan team, warning that the association risked becoming complicit in sportswashing—the practice of using sports to improve a reputation tarnished by human rights abuses—by accepting money from a government that systematically abuses human rights. The senators gave the NBA until 2 November to provide a written response regarding its continued partnership with Rwanda, questioning how the association could reconcile the partnership with its commitment to justice.

The US imposed sanctions on the Rwandan army and the country's defence ministry in March, accusing the military of fueling conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Specifically, the US cited support for the M23 rebel group, which has seized control of large parts of eastern DR Congo. Although Rwanda denies backing the rebels, the US maintains there is overwhelming evidence of such support.

cards.headline: U.S. Supreme Court denies Trump administration request to block California ballot counting

pages.text: The U.S. Supreme Court denied a request from the Donald Trump administration to temporarily block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters on November 2, 2026. Federal officials alleged these voters are likely non-U.S. citizens. The decision occurred on the eve of the U.S. midterm elections. The court issued its ruling in a brief, one-sentence order that offered no explanation for the decision and included no publicly noted dissents among the justices. The justices reached this conclusion in six hours and 24 minutes, a period of time noted for its speed compared to the institution's typical decision-making process, which usually spans weeks or months.

cards.headline: Oil prices fall as hopes rise for breakthrough to end Iran war

pages.text: Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil, dropped by more than 6.5% to as low as $105.55 a barrel, its lowest level since 16 October. The price decline follows reports of ongoing contacts between Iran and the United States aimed at ending their eight-month war in the Middle East. This drop in oil prices has sparked hopes for a reduction in global inflationary pressures, while also driving airline shares higher and pushing down government borrowing costs.

Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi stated, according to the state media outlet IRNA, that consultations through mediators are “very intensive.” Araghchi said that Iran has presented its conditions and proposals, noting that “everything depends on the political rationality of Washington.” Investors were also encouraged by reports that Iran’s supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, had granted “powers” to his government regarding its talks with the US to end the conflict. Over the weekend, Qatari officials attempted to negotiate the release of more than $6bn (£4.5bn) in Iranian assets to potentially allow the Strait of Hormuz to reopen.

US vice-president JD Vance reported having had “a number of good conversations with the Iranians” and expressed optimism regarding the prospects of a “negotiated settlement.” Vance sent a letter to Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, though the White House has provided few details regarding the letter's contents. This follows a more belligerent tone from Donald Trump, who told voters in Iowa on 2026-11-01 that Iran would receive “the hammer” unless progress is made. Trump stated during a campaign rally that while he wants to save lives, he may eventually have to “give them the hammer.” Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at the investing and trading platform IG, described the news as “manna from heaven” for pressured stock markets, but noted a remaining risk that Trump may take further action after the midterms.

cards.headline: Iranian Supreme Leader warns US political shifts will not end hostility toward Iran

pages.text: Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated that anyone expecting a change in United States policy toward Iran due to US political shifts is “seriously mistaken.” His comments followed US midterm elections in which Democrats gained control of both chambers of Congress, dealing a blow to President Donald Trump and the Republican Party. While other Iranian officials reacted to the Republican defeat with a more optimistic tone, Khamenei issued a warning that partisan or factional shifts in the US would not dissuade Washington from its hostility toward the Iranian nation. He also stated that making concessions to the United States would not change its behavior toward Iran.

Khamenei’s statement, published on his website, coincided with the National Day of the Fight Against Global Arrogance, an annual observance on November 4 marking the anniversary of the 1979 seizure of the US embassy in Tehran. In his message, the Supreme Leader claimed that Iran’s control of the Strait of Hormuz—a waterway through which one fifth of the world’s oil and gas passed before the war—had shattered the “myth of America’s invincibility.” He described the elimination of US military bases in regional countries as a reaction to US “aggression and crimes” during the conflict. Khamenei warned that any renewed US attack would draw a “far wider response” and that repeated transgressions would take on “much wider dimensions.”

President Trump acknowledged that the US-Israel war on Iran, which began in February, likely contributed to the poor performance of the Republican Party in the elections. Trump suggested that voters were likely not prepared for the “short-term consequence of paying more for gasoline.” Al Jazeera’s Resul Serdar Atas, reporting from Tehran, noted that Khamenei’s cautious stance regarding US policy contrasted with the more celebratory mood expressed by other Iranian officials following the midterm results.

cards.headline: Niger signs cooperation agreement with eastern Libya's military commander

pages.text: Niger signed a memorandum of understanding with Khalifa Haftar, the military commander of eastern Libya, on November 1, 2026, to strengthen bilateral relations. The agreement aims to expand cooperation in various fields and was approved by Nigerien Prime Minister Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine during a visit to Benghazi alongside several political and military officials. Benghazi serves as the de facto capital of eastern Libya, which is controlled by General Haftar and his clan. Niger shares a border of more than 340 kilometres with Libya. While Niger maintains relations with both Libyan authorities, the visit marks a rapprochement with the administration in Benghazi.

Since 2014, Libya has been divided between the UN-recognised government in Tripoli, led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah, and a rival administration in the east. The country has faced instability since the 2011 overthrow of longtime ruler Muammar Gaddafi during a NATO-backed uprising. In an effort to reunify the country, Turkey recently hosted talks in Ankara between military officials and diplomats from both Libya's eastern and western administrations. A senior Turkish official stated that these discussions have focused primarily on military unification, with political unity expected to be addressed at a later stage.

cards.headline: Palace of Westminster faces risk of 'Notre Dame-style fire' as renovation costs rise

pages.text: The Palace of Westminster faces the risk of a catastrophic fire or similar disaster if lawmakers do not address funding for refurbishments, according to a report by the cross-party Commons public accounts committee (PAC). The committee warned that the Grade I-listed and Unesco world heritage site is at risk of a fire similar to the one that affected Notre Dame, driven largely by outdated electrics that currently necessitate 24-hour fire patrols. Sir Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, the Conservative MP who chairs the PAC, stated that these are “real and rising risks” rather than “notional possibilities.” He noted that a catastrophic failure could damage the UK's morale and reputation, potentially resulting in the destruction of heritage, injuries, or loss of life.

The Victorian estate is currently struggling with ongoing maintenance issues, including leaking roofs, crumbling masonry protected by scaffolding, and regular plumbing failures. Maintenance costs are approximately £1.5m a week, but the PAC report stated that without action, this figure is expected to reach £2m a week. Decisions regarding the timing and method of a full restoration have been repeatedly delayed due to spiralling costs and disagreements over how the work should be conducted. The PAC estimated that every year of inaction adds approximately £420m to the total restoration programme. A recent estimate found that the full work could cost as much as £40bn and potentially last for six decades.

cards.headline: Lebanese Prime Minister warns against 'reckless adventure' following Iran leader's remarks

pages.text: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam warned against dragging Lebanon into a new “reckless adventure” in the service of foreign interests. His comments followed remarks by Iran’s supreme leader that renewed fears in Lebanon that Hezbollah could involve the country in a fresh regional conflict. Salam made the warning after meeting with President Joseph Aoun, stating that Lebanon cannot afford the consequences of being thrust into confrontations.

The Prime Minister emphasized that Lebanese citizens, particularly those in the south, have already paid a heavy price regarding their lives, livelihoods, and homes. Salam stated that these citizens have the right to live in safety and build futures away from cycles of war, displacement, and destruction. He characterized the protection of Lebanon as a national responsibility that requires prioritizing the country's supreme interests and ensuring that decisions regarding war and peace remain exclusively with the state and its constitutional institutions.

cards.headline: Alberta Premier says government will prepare legal defense if NDP challenges electoral boundary report

pages.text: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith stated her government will assemble a legal team to argue that proposed new electoral boundaries achieve effective representation if the Opposition NDP pursues a legal challenge. Smith told reporters at the Rural Municipalities of Alberta convention that she hopes the matter is resolved through legislative debate rather than court proceedings. The dispute follows a November 2, 2026, report from an advisory panel regarding Alberta’s electoral boundaries. The Alberta NDP has stated it will take the new maps to court on constitutional grounds, with Opposition Leader Naheed Nenshi specifically calling the Lethbridge proposal illegal and unconstitutional.

The advisory panel's report proposed several changes, including expanding some Calgary ridings across municipal boundaries and establishing one sole urban seat for Lethbridge alongside three hybrid urban-rural seats. The controversy involves the principle of effective representation, a legal standard that allows for the balancing of equal-sized voter populations with other factors such as geography. While the panel's chair, retired Alberta Court of Appeal justice Brian O’Ferrall, wrote in an executive summary that he did not believe the proposals were unconstitutional, a minority of the panel disagreed. Panel members Gerard Kennedy, a constitutional law professor at the University of Alberta, and Brent Robinson, a former Okotoks councillor, wrote that they expected the courts would become involved.

cards.headline: Syria says it foiled Hezbollah-linked plot to bomb Homs refinery

pages.text: Syrian domestic intelligence and security forces reported on November 1, 2026, that they prevented a terrorist plot targeting the Homs refinery in central Syria. Authorities stated the plot was carried out by a cell affiliated with the Hezbollah militia. Security forces said they arrested two members of the cell and seized explosives intended for the attack. The Homs refinery is currently the only operational refinery in Syria, as another facility at Banias on the coast is undergoing maintenance. This follows a series of unclaimed attacks against oil and gas pipelines in various parts of Syria, including sabotage attacks against an oil pipeline and a gas pipeline reported by Damascus in early October. Hezbollah denied the accusations in their entirety, stating the group has no presence or connections in Syrian territory and is not involved in activities undermining Syria's security and stability. The Lebanese group previously fought alongside the since-overthrown Bashar al-Assad during Syria's civil war, which ended in late 2024, and has earned ongoing enmity from those now in power in Damascus. Damascus has previously announced the dismantling of cells linked to Hezbollah, an allegation the group has denied each time. Despite the tension, Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa and Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem have both raised the possibility of meeting.

cards.headline: Former Royal Bank of Canada employee found guilty of fraud and identity theft after accessing Prime Minister Mark Carney’s data

pages.text: Ibrahim El-Hakim, a former Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) employee at a downtown Ottawa branch, has been found guilty of three criminal charges after opening fraudulent accounts and viewing the personal banking information of Prime Minister Mark Carney. El-Hakim pleaded guilty in August to fraud over $5,000, unauthorized use of a computer, and identity theft, according to court documents filed in Ontario. An agreed statement of facts in the case states that El-Hakim opened at least 43 fraudulent accounts at the bank between November 2023 and June 2025. The RCMP launched an investigation following a complaint from RBC. A sentencing hearing was delayed because El-Hakim did not appear; his lawyer informed Ontario Court Justice Norm Boxall that El-Hakim was no longer in Ottawa. The court has scheduled a new date for sentencing.

According to the agreed statement of facts, El-Hakim was recruited via Telegram, a social media messaging app, by an individual using the alias AI WORLD. El-Hakim stated he believed the recruiter was associated with organized crime and that he participated in the scheme because he was experiencing financial difficulties. El-Hakim described creating bank profiles and opening credit products after receiving instructions and personal identifying information from AI WORLD. This information included names, dates of birth, social insurance numbers, driver’s licence information, passport data, and customer profile information.

cards.headline: Syrian President Ahmad Al Shara meets Saudi Crown Prince in Riyadh

pages.text: Syrian President Ahmad Al Shara met Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh for his second visit to the kingdom in weeks. According to a report from the Syrian state news agency Sana, the leaders discussed bilateral relations, ways to strengthen cooperation across various fields, and regional and international developments of mutual interest. The two leaders also stressed the importance of promoting security and stability in the region. Al Shara arrived in the Saudi capital with a high-level delegation including the foreign, defence, finance, and industry ministers, as well as the head of the General Intelligence Directorate. This follows a previous visit by Al Shara to Riyadh on October 6, where he also met Prince Mohammed to discuss bilateral relations and opportunities for development.

The meeting occurs as Syria explores potential integration into the Makkah defence agreement. Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Al Shibani recently stated at the Manama Dialogue in Bahrain that Damascus considers security in the Gulf to be part of its own. Al Shibani noted that there have been “some negotiations” regarding Syria joining the pact, though he added that Syria would support any organization protecting regional security regardless of whether it joins the agreement. The Makkah defence agreement, signed in August between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey, stipulates that an attack on one member is viewed as an attack on all. This discussion on regional deterrence follows recent drone and missile attacks by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis against Saudi Arabian airports, military sites, and oil facilities.

cards.headline: Muslim Votes Matter softens anti-Labor stance to defeat One Nation in Victorian election

pages.text: The grassroots advocacy group Muslim Votes Matter (MVM) will relax its anti-Labor position for the Victorian state election on 28 November, deploying volunteers to Labor-held outer suburban seats to prevent One Nation from gaining influence. The group intends to direct supporters to vote for Labor ahead of Pauline Hanson’s party in all lower house Victorian electorates. MVM aims to place volunteers in the seats of Greenvale in Melbourne’s north and Narre Warren South in the city’s south-east, areas the group fears could be seized by One Nation. This strategy marks a departure from the group's position during the 2025 federal election, when the pro-Palestine organization endorsed Greens and independent candidates to punish Labor over the federal government's handling of Israel’s war in Gaza.

Ghaith Krayem, the national spokesperson for MVM, stated that “circumstances have changed” ahead of the state election. While the group will direct votes toward Labor over One Nation, Krayem said MVM will not place Labor in the top spot on its how-to-vote cards in any seat, continuing to favor independents and minor parties as it did at the 2025 federal election. Krayem noted that a hard anti-Labor stance could benefit One Nation, an outcome the community does not want. MVM also plans to preference Labor over the Liberal party in seats where preferences from the Liberal party could flow to One Nation. Krayem expressed concerns that if the Coalition is unable to form a majority government, it might be forced to negotiate with One Nation and agree to its policy demands, citing Pauline Hanson's calls for a burqa ban as rhetoric that affects Muslim people.

cards.headline: B.C. privacy watchdog investigates Crime Stoppers following massive data breach

pages.text: The Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner for B.C. (OIPC) has launched an investigation into whether the provincial Crime Stoppers society took reasonable steps to safeguard personal information under the Personal Information Protection Act. The probe follows a massive data breach across Canada that exposed more than 1.5 million tips submitted to Canadian Crime Stoppers programs over the last 25 years, according to a CBC investigation. Crime Stoppers is a network of civilian-run non-profits that collects anonymous tips on crime and suspicious activity to assist law enforcement investigations while promising anonymity to tipsters.

The hacktivist collective Internet Yiff Machine stole the data. In a manifesto, the group stated it intended to disprove claims made by P3 Global Intel—the company hired by Crime Stoppers to manage its tips—that the platform was secure and anonymous. Many of the compromised tips involved serious allegations, with some individuals explicitly stating they feared retribution for speaking out. A third of all tips concerned drugs and drug trafficking, while hundreds of reports regarding suspicious neighborhood activity named individuals and implicated organized crime groups, including the Hells Angels, Rock Machine, Outlaws, B.C.’s Red Scorpions, and Independent Soldiers.

cards.headline: Farmers in Ghana's Ahafo region demand unpaid compensation for Newmont mining project lands

pages.text: The Concerned Farmers Association of Afrispakrom, Terchire, Susuanso, and Adrobaa in the Tano North Municipality of the Ahafo region is calling on the Land Valuation Division of the Lands Commission to immediately pay outstanding compensation for lands, crops, and farm structures. These properties were acquired for Newmont Ghana Gold Ltd’s Ahafo North mining project under Executive Instrument (E.I.) 273 of 2024. At a news conference in Terchire on November 2, 2026, the Association rejected claims by Newmont that certain farm structures are “speculative,” a classification Newmont is using to halt compensation payments. The dispute centers on which legal framework governs how land is acquired and how property values are assessed. In June 2026, the Lands Commission notified the Association that Newmont had petitioned to deny compensation to 21 farmers, arguing that their structures should be excluded based on a 2017 cut-off date found in the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703). The Association argues this mining law is inapplicable because the state used the Land Act, 2020 (Act 1036) to compulsorily acquire the lands. Under Act 1036, land improvements are only considered speculative if they were built after the formal publication of the state's notice of acquisition, and the law contains no such 2017 cut-off date.

The Association noted that all contested structures underwent a physical inspection, counting, and verification during a 2024 joint exercise supervised by a Ministerial Committee. Valuation records from that exercise were formally signed by representatives of the Land Valuation Division, Newmont, and the affected farmers. Following this, the Lands Commission's Valuation Technical Committee approved compensation figures on April 13, 2026, which the farmers' legal team accepted on April 24, 2026. Beyond the current dispute, the Association highlighted that members remain unpaid for a separate acquisition under E.I. 356 of 2023, issued on September 29, 2023. State authorities took possession of those lands in December 2023 and destroyed the properties, leaving farmers without compensation or livelihoods for nearly three years. John Mensah, Chairman of the farmers, stated that Newmont is the beneficiary of the acquisition rather than the State and must not take over the Lands Commission's responsibility to assess and pay compensation according to the law. Joseph Adu Yaw, Secretary of the Association, said the loss of farms has caused family hardship, noting that some members have died or become ill while waiting for payment. The Association is demanding a clear written explanation of outstanding issues and a definite timetable for payment.

cards.headline: Ghana’s 20 national teams rely on one broken bus, says GFA President

cards.headline: Ghana inflation rises to 5.5% in October 2026

pages.text: Ghana’s year-on-year inflation rate increased to 5.5% in October 2026, up from 5.2% in September. This represents the third consecutive monthly rise since July. Government Statistician Dr. Alhassan Iddrisu reported the finding while presenting the October 2026 Consumer Price Index and Inflation Report, noting that the increase was largely influenced by rising prices in the services sector. Non-food inflation remains a primary driver of the increase, accounting for approximately 76% of the overall inflation rate, while food inflation accounted for 24%.

Dr. Iddrisu explained that for every one Ghana cedi price rise in October 2026, about 76 pesewas came from non-food items and 24 pesewas came from food. Services inflation rose to 11.5% from 8.3% in September, while goods inflation declined to 3.8% from 4.2%. Dr. Iddrisu noted that services are now experiencing price increases at a pace approximately three times faster than goods. Transport recorded the highest inflation among the 13 expenditure divisions, rising to 14.1% in October from 5.7% in September, with transport prices increasing by 8% within the month. Housing, water, electricity, gas, and other fuels recorded 10.5% inflation, making that division the single largest contributor to October's inflation at 24.4%.

In contrast to the overall rise, food inflation eased to 2.8% in October, down from 4% in September and 9.5% in October 2025. On a month-on-month basis, food prices declined by 2%, contributing to an overall 0.1% reduction in prices between September and October.

cards.headline: Economists criticize Woodfibre LNG economic impact study for 'massive exaggeration'

pages.text: Economists are questioning the accuracy of an economic impact assessment study commissioned by Woodfibre LNG (WLNG), calling the findings a massive exaggeration of expected GDP and employment growth. The study, conducted by the Vancouver-based strategy advisory firm Deetken Insight, claims the construction of the WLNG facility and the FortisBC Eagle Mountain Pipeline will contribute around $7 billion in GDP and generate nearly $13.6 billion in total economic output. It also projects the construction will support over 52,000 job-years and approximately $3.6 billion in labour income. Marc Lee, a senior economist with the Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives, stated that the study makes assumptions at nearly every turn that make the numbers much larger than they should be.

Discrepancies have been noted between the Deetken study and Woodfibre LNG's own communications regarding employment. While the Deetken study projects the facility alone will generate 18,145 direct job-years, Woodfibre LNG's website states that 1,500 workers will be on-site at the peak of construction. Marc Lee noted that with a four-year building average of 1,500 workers on site, the total would be 6,000 job-years, which does not align with the study's figures. The Woodfibre LNG project is under construction at the site of an old pulp mill approximately seven kilometres southwest of Squamish in Howe Sound, British Columbia. The facility is designed to process and liquefy natural gas shipped by pipeline from northern B.C. for export to Asian markets. The study claims construction at the WLNG site will be more than 70 per cent complete as of September 2026.

cards.headline: Canada's auditor general reports persistent weaknesses in Nunavut foster care

pages.text: A follow-up report from the office of the auditor general of Canada states that many fundamental weaknesses in Nunavut's foster care system remain, more than three years after an urgent call to action was issued to improve the territory's child and family services. The 36-page report details how the territorial government is failing to maintain proper oversight of children in care to ensure their safety and well-being. Deputy auditor general Andrew Hayes said during a news conference in Iqaluit that the department has known about these issues for the better part of 15 years, noting that problems were first raised in an audit in 2011 and again in 2023.

The audit, which focused on the period between November 2024 and this past March, found that foster homes were not being properly screened or monitored. Additionally, caregivers were not receiving important background or health information regarding the children in their care, and training for new caregivers was described as little or infrequent. The report stated that without these basic safeguards, the department could not consistently assure itself that the needs of children in foster care were being met or that they were safe. Investigators noted they could not obtain a representative sample of all children in foster care due to the unreliability of the department's reporting and data on children in the system.

To conduct the investigation, officials reviewed documents, interviewed workers in the Department of Family Services, and met with foster caregivers. They also reviewed a sample of 40 foster home files. Andrew Hayes stated that the same problems are being seen all across the territory and called for a whole-of-government approach to support children and families. He indicated there is a long road ahead for the department to resolve its many problems.

cards.headline: Garment factories in Bangladesh shut as workers clash with police over wage demands

pages.text: Garment workers in Bangladesh have clashed with police while protesting for higher minimum wages, leading to the closure of hundreds of factories. The unrest has disrupted an industry that employs approximately 4 million people and generates about $40 billion in annual export earnings. On November 4, 2026, more than 100 garment factories in the industrial areas of Savar and Ashulia declared holidays due to the labor unrest, according to Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of Ashulia Industrial Police-1. Protesters are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($243–$245), which would be a 140 percent increase from the current 12,500 taka. Workers stated that rising costs for food, housing, transport, and healthcare have eroded their purchasing power amid 8 percent inflation.

Clashes between security forces and protesters occurred in several areas, including Savar, Ashulia, Gazipur, and Narayanganj. In the Padmar Mor area, Dhaka police superintendent Shamima Parveen reported that approximately 30,000 to 40,000 workers gathered and attacked police, resulting in the burning of a vehicle used by the officer-in-charge of Savar Model Police Station. The officer-in-charge was seriously injured in the attack. Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse crowds, and one person was detained in the Hemayetpur area with a crude bomb. Additionally, several journalists were reportedly injured during the unrest, including Nazmul Huda, president of the Savar Press Club, who was assaulted while conducting a live broadcast.

The government formed a six-member wage board on November 1, 2026, to review the workers' demands. Despite this, protests have continued, with industry representatives noting that at least 670 factories saw workers walk out on November 2, 2026. Police spokesperson Kamarum Munira stated that 58 officers have been injured since the protests began, and cases have been filed against thousands of unidentified protesters for property damage and torching vehicles. While workers argue they must take to the streets to secure a living wage, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed warned that those attempting to destabilize the country under the guise of labor protests will be dealt with firmly. Factory owners have noted that the industry faces higher costs and slowing demand in export markets.

cards.headline: New payment scheme rewards Botswana communities for coexistence with wildlife

pages.text: Two rural communities on the edge of Botswana’s Okavango Delta are receiving payments through a new scheme that rewards residents for living alongside wildlife. Under the Harmony with Wildlife program, residents earn money from photographs of animals such as elephants and lions that may raid vegetable gardens or kill livestock. The program is a partnership between the conservation nonprofit Wild Impact, safari company &Beyond, and the remote villages of Gogomoga and Tsutsubega. Each of these two villages has fewer than 500 residents and lacks paved roads, schools, shops, or electricity. The Okavango Delta is home to approximately 130,000 people, including Indigenous San communities, as well as hippos, elephants, and large predators.

The incentive model grew from efforts to document wildlife damage. In April 2024, local rangers began helping residents record damage caused by wild animals so they could seek compensation from Botswana’s wildlife department. This led to the installation of camera traps to track the movement of elephants and other large mammals. Wild Impact CEO Andrew Venter stated that wildlife commonly enters villages, noting that elephants can eat crops and damage water boreholes. Venter said the communities have been “remarkably tolerant” of wildlife. After two years of monitoring footage, Wild Impact developed the payment model to acknowledge the community's role in conservation and promote coexistence. Residents worked with Wild Impact to deploy the cameras in a manner that does not interfere with privacy.

cards.headline: Community surveys in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, identify barriers to Bundibugyo virus disease response

pages.text: A rapid survey conducted from 10 to 18 August 2026 in the Nizi health zone of Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, identified social and cultural factors that hindered the response to a Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic. The survey, supported by the World Health Organization (WHO), aimed to understand why community members were reluctant to seek medical care and why many deaths occurred outside of clinical settings. Nina Gobat, a WHO community survey officer in the response team, stated the goal was to understand the causes behind the refusal of life-saving interventions. Bundibugyo virus disease is a viral illness that can cause fever and vomiting, and the survey found that low suspicion of the disease at the onset of the outbreak facilitated its transmission.

The Nizi health zone was among the first areas affected by the epidemic. Dr. Jean Claude Lonzama, Chief Medical Officer of the Nizi health zone, recalled that the first case was recorded in May, a few days before the official declaration of the outbreak, with an increase in suspected cases by the end of May. The outbreak reached its most critical level in July, when the zone reported 827 confirmed cases and 488 deaths. Of those deaths, 59% occurred in the community. During the outbreak, families resisted dignified and safe burials and refused to seek care in Ebola treatment centres.

The rapid assessment revealed that initial symptoms—including headache, fever, abdominal pain, and vomiting—were non-specific, leading affected individuals to self-diagnose without considering Bundibugyo virus disease as a possibility. Common care pathways included self-medication, recourse to traditional healers, and home care, which was often provided by women. According to the assessment, these practices delayed access to appropriate care and posed a high risk of ongoing transmission.

cards.headline: Campaigners urge UK government to cut firework noise limits to 90 decibels to protect wildlife

pages.text: The Center for Wild Animal Welfare (CWAW) is calling on the UK government to reduce the maximum noise level of fireworks sold to the public from 120 decibels (dB) to 90 dB to protect millions of wild animals from acute stress. The CWAW argues that a 90 dB limit would reduce the area disturbed by each firework to approximately 100 times smaller than the area affected under the government's current proposal to lower the limit to 110 dB. While the government recently consulted on a plan to halve the loudness of fireworks by moving the limit from 120 dB to 110 dB, campaigners contend this does not go far enough to prevent harm to wildlife. Reducing the limit to 90 dB—which is about one-eighth the loudness of 120 dB—could help prevent mass temporary displacement and fatal collisions among birds during displays.

Richard Parr, the director of the CWAW, explained that because decibels operate on a logarithmic scale, every 10-decibel reduction in the limit reduces the noise-affected area by 10 times. Parr noted that loud fireworks can travel up to 10km and stated that while the distress caused by fireworks to pets is widely recognized, there is insufficient awareness regarding the impact on wild animals. He suggested the effects on wildlife might be worse than on pets because the sudden, unexpected noises disrupt natural life rhythms and can be particularly terrifying for jumpy prey animals. Rebecca Machin, a wildlife expert at the RSPCA, shared these concerns, noting that fireworks and their debris can cause suffering, elevated stress hormones, disrupted migration, and physical hazards for various wild animals, particularly birds.

cards.headline: World's tallest Day of the Dead skeleton sets record in Mexico City

pages.text: A massive female skeleton known as La Catrina, standing a little more than 109 feet tall, has set a new Guinness World Record in Mexico City. The installation, which is roughly the height of an 11-story building, surpassed the previous record of 92 feet set in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, in 2023. The figure, dressed in a long purple gown, was displayed in the city's main square, the Zócalo, during recent Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) celebrations on November 1 and 2. While the temporary installation was originally scheduled to stand through November 2, Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada revealed on social media that the statue will remain on view through November 11.

More than 140 people with the Xibalbá art workshop, led by director Carlos Camilo Báez, used steel, fiberglass, and papier-mâché to construct La Catrina and her 88-foot-long dress. The statue is surrounded by a large memorial altar, or ofrenda, which features an estimated 70,000 marigold plants grown in the city’s Xochimilco borough. Día de los Muertos is a festive occasion observed primarily in Mexico and other parts of Latin America that celebrates the connection between the living and the dead. The holiday, which was inscribed to UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity list in 2008, blends Indigenous traditions with Catholic influences. During the holiday, families often create altars decorated with candles, photographs, marigolds, and favorite foods to help guide the spirits of deceased loved ones home.

cards.headline: Elon Musk jokes about Republican defeat after spending nearly half a billion dollars on US midterm elections

pages.text: Tech billionaire Elon Musk joked on X that his “election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time” following the Republican Party's defeat in the November 3, 2026, US midterm elections. Musk, the founder of Tesla and SpaceX, reportedly spent $446 million supporting Republican candidates, making him the largest individual contributor in a federal election cycle since unlimited election spending was permitted in 2010. According to campaign finance tracker OpenSecrets, his donations primarily went to his Republican-leaning America PAC and the Republican Senate Leadership Fund (SLF) super PAC. A super PAC is a political action committee that can raise unlimited sums of money from corporations, unions, and individuals to spend on elections, provided it does not coordinate directly with candidates. On the same day, Democrats seized control of the US Congress by capturing both the Senate and the House of Representatives.

The Republican defeat included losses in states considered strongholds, such as Texas and Kansas. In Texas, Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton, a close ally of Donald Trump. Talarico became the first Democrat to win statewide office in Texas since 1994. The SLF used $158 million of Musk's donations in September to support Paxton's campaign. During a victory rally in Austin, Talarico characterized the race as a fight against “Goliaths,” specifically naming the “richest man in the world” and the “most powerful man in the world.” Voters rejected Paxton’s plan to establish Texas as a center for the artificial intelligence industry through rapid data center construction, as Talarico campaigned for tighter regulations on such developments. Musk responded to the loss on X by writing, “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now.”

Musk also supported the Republican candidate for Governor of Texas, but the Democrats won that race as well. Gina Hinojosa defeated incumbent Governor Greg Abbott, despite a $5 million donation from Musk to the Republican candidate. Musk, who became a trillionaire in June when SpaceX went public, has moved the headquarters of Tesla, SpaceX, and X to Texas. The scale of Musk's spending follows a 2010 Supreme Court ruling that prevents the government from limiting political spending by corporations, unions, and other groups if the spending is done independently of candidates.

cards.headline: Former prisoners recount broken marriages and family rejection at reintegration conference

pages.text: Former prisoners shared accounts of abandoned families, broken marriages, and rejection by loved ones following their release from prison during the first-ever National Ex-Convicts Reintegration Conference. The Crime Check Foundation, which organized the event, is calling for former prisoners to be recognized as returning citizens rather than being labeled as ex-convicts. Participants stated that the stigma of imprisonment has made it difficult to secure employment, find stable accommodation, and restore relationships after serving sentences.

One former prisoner reported that his wife left him due to his prison history, leaving him to struggle to provide for himself and his children. He observed that while society often encourages inmates to reform while in prison, it frequently fails to provide a fair chance upon their return, allowing past mistakes to continue defining them.

The lack of support and ongoing rejection can push former prisoners back into difficult circumstances, which undermines efforts to help them become responsible members of society. cards.headline: 4.1-billion-year-old Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 identified as one of the oldest ever found

pages.text: Scientists have identified Teghaza 001, an 800g rose-coloured Martian meteorite found on a salt plain in Mali in 2022, as one of the oldest Martian meteorites ever discovered on Earth. The rock dates back approximately 4.1 billion years, making it roughly the same age as the previous record-holder, ALH84001, and approximately two billion years older than the next-oldest contender, Black Beauty. While ALH84001 is composed of a single mineral, Teghaza 001 features a variety of igneous materials, which allowed researchers to determine its origins on Mars. Because its balance of different minerals, specifically zircon, closely matches those found in the southern highlands of Mars, a team of scientists was able to pinpoint its origin to one of 11 specific locations. The meteorite provides evidence of how the Martian crust formed from cooling magma before being altered by subsurface water.

Two separate teams of NASA scientists analyzed the meteorite. One team focused on the rock's water content and published findings in the journal Science Advances in June 2026. A second team, led by Yang Liu and Lee Saper from NASA-JPL and NASA’s Ames Research Center, published results in the journal Science on 29 October. This second team revealed the meteorite's extreme age using a technique called in-situ rubidium-strontium dating. Deployed by Francois Tissot of Caltech, this method allowed researchers to date the sample without dissolving and analyzing the entire specimen.

cards.headline: Research identifies enzyme as potential factor in Angelman Syndrome brain impacts

pages.text: A study published in the journal Nature by Jason Yi, Ph.D., an assistant professor in the Department of Neuroscience at WashU Medicine, suggests that the enzyme asparagine synthetase (ASNS) plays an important role in how Angelman Syndrome impacts the brain. Previously, researchers assumed ASNS was a mundane metabolic enzyme used only for general cellular housekeeping, but Yi's research indicates the protein is expressed specifically in the neurons of the brain, matching the expression pattern of the UBE3A gene associated with the disorder. This finding may provide insight into how the disease affects biological systems and could identify ASNS as a potential therapeutic target for future treatments.

Angelman Syndrome is a neuro-genetic disorder affecting approximately 1 in 20,000 births, impacting movement, sleep, and cognitive function. While patients often live as long as others, the disease causes significant difficulties, including seizures, intellectual disability, and speech impairment. There is currently no cure. The disorder is caused by the loss of the maternal copy of the UBE3A gene in neurons, a phenomenon driven by genomic imprinting—a process where certain genes are expressed in a parent-of-origin-specific manner. While the role of UBE3A is known, the specific mechanism of how its loss impacts biological systems has remained elusive.

cards.headline: Companion star Siwarha may be traveling through Betelgeuse's atmosphere

pages.text: New evidence suggests the companion star Siwarha is traveling through the atmosphere of Betelgeuse, a massive red supergiant in the constellation Orion. Astronomers detected subtle changes in the shape of Betelgeuse's outer layers, indicating that something is moving through the surrounding gas and disturbing it. This discovery follows observations from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) and the U.S. National Science Foundation's Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (NSF VLA), which revealed that Betelgeuse's vast outer atmosphere has largely returned to normal after previous disturbances.

Betelgeuse, which forms the shoulder of the hunter in the Orion constellation, attracted global attention during the Great Dimming in late 2019 and early 2020. During that period, the star's brightness unexpectedly dropped to its lowest recorded level in more than 100 years, leading researchers to investigate the internal processes of the aging star. The current research, led by Dr. Matthews, a Principal Research Scientist and Assistant Director at MIT Haystack Observatory, suggests the presence of Siwarha as a likely cause for the physical disturbances in the giant star's atmosphere. Dr. Matthews worked with scientists from the European Southern Observatory, the University of Manchester, and the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian on the study.

cards.headline: Long-term study reveals jaguars in Brazil exhibit complex social lives

pages.text: A 13-year study of jaguars in the Pantanal, the world’s largest tropical wetland area in the Brazilian state of Mato Grosso do Sul, suggests these cats have more complex social lives than previously thought. While widely regarded as solitary predators, research published in the journal Animal Behaviour indicates that their interactions are not dominated by aggression. Researchers from the Jaguar Identification Project, supported by the University of Florida, the University of Mato Grosso in Brazil, Panthera, the World Wildlife Fund (WWF), and citizen scientists, conducted the study in the region, which hosts the highest density of jaguars on the planet. The Northern Pantanal provided a setting where an abundance of aquatic and terrestrial prey allows for more frequent interactions that do not escalate into conflict.

The research utilized the largest long-term dataset of directly observed jaguar interactions, having identified 459 individual jaguars. Based on 1,710 days of systematic river-based surveys in the settlement of Porto Jofre, researchers documented 167 social interaction events involving 69 individual jaguars. Abigail Martin, the Jaguar Identification Project director and a co-author of the study, stated that years of identifying individuals and following family relationships allowed for questions about social behaviour to be asked that short-term studies cannot answer. Of the recorded interactions, 24.5 per cent were interpreted as agonistic, meaning they were related to struggle, contest, or conflict. The remaining interactions were 36.5 per cent neutral and 38.9 per cent affiliative, which included behaviors such as eating, resting, moving, grooming, hunting, or playing together. Nearly 68 per cent of those affiliative interactions occurred between related individuals, most often related males.

cards.headline: Stanford scientists use AI to identify naturally occurring molecule for potential weight loss medication

pages.text: Scientists at Stanford Medicine have identified a naturally occurring molecule, known as BRP, that could lead to a new generation of weight loss medications. Using artificial intelligence to search through thousands of possible biological compounds, researchers found that BRP may suppress appetite and promote fat loss in a manner similar to semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic. Early animal experiments suggest BRP could potentially avoid some of the side effects associated with current treatments, such as nausea, constipation, or substantial muscle loss. The researchers have begun preparing to determine if the molecule is safe and effective in humans.

BRP functions differently than existing treatments like semaglutide by acting more selectively on the hypothalamus, a small region deep within the brain that regulates hunger, energy use, body temperature, and other functions necessary to maintain internal balance. Katrin Svensson, PhD, an assistant professor of pathology at Stanford, noted that the receptors targeted by semaglutide are found in the brain as well as in the gut, pancreas, and other tissues. This widespread presence is why Ozempic can cause effects such as lowering blood sugar levels and slowing the movement of food through the digestive tract. In contrast, BRP appears to act specifically in the hypothalamus, which controls appetite and metabolism.
